title: A new home page and a faster way to add flights
items: The home page has a new design. It shows an example flight log on a world map, a globe that replays a trip as you scroll, and what each part of FlyLog shows you.
Adding a flight has three tabs. Describe your trip in your own words and the AI fills in the flights, use the form, or import a CSV file from your computer.
The form asks for the route first, with a button to swap the two airports. Arrival time and cabin class sit in an optional section, and connecting and return flights are one tap away.
When you install FlyLog on your phone or computer, the install window now shows screenshots of the app.
The home page loads faster on phones, and it no longer flashes plain text before it appears.

title: Flight details, runway times and a new Route tour
items: Open a flight to see it as a boarding pass, in a sheet that slides up from the bottom on phones.
The flight status shows delays as chips such as "17 min late", with the terminal, gate, check-in desk and aircraft registration when the airline publishes them.
When the data is available, the status also shows the take-off and landing times on the runway, the time in the air and the baggage belt.
Deleting a flight asks you to confirm in place, so you cannot remove one by accident.
The Route tour plays the flights your filters leave, oldest first. A boarding pass under the globe shows the current flight, with a slider to jump to any flight and three playback speeds.
The Route tour works in dark mode.

title: A new sign-in page
items: Sign in or create an account on a card designed as a boarding pass, with Google first and email below.
A show password button reveals both password fields when you sign up, so you can check they match.
Error messages are clearer, for example when an email and password do not match.

title: A new Flights list, Timeline and Badges
items: The Flights list shows each flight as a compact row, grouped by year.
Search the list by city, airport code, airline or flight number. Type two cities to find the flights between them.
Sort your flights by date or by distance.
A new account shows a blank boarding pass with three ways to add your first flight.
The Timeline shows every month you have flown as a calendar heatmap, newest year on top. Switch it between flights, kilometres and CO₂e, and tap a month to see its total.
The Badges page shows each badge as a boarding pass with the date you earned it or how far you have to go, and a Closest next card tells you which badge you will earn soonest.

title: A new look, built for phones
items: FlyLog has a new design, with a tab bar at the bottom of the screen on phones and an add button that is always in reach.
The Stats page opens on your map, with your next or last flight as a boarding pass, your longest and shortest flights, and your charts.
All stats lists every number about your flights, including how many times your distance would go around the Earth or to the Moon.
One filter panel now filters the Stats and Flights pages, and the filters you picked show as tags.
Choose a light or dark appearance, or follow your device, from the account menu.

title: Cabin class, aircraft and automatic status checks
items: Record the cabin class of each flight. CO₂ estimates now use a different factor for each cabin.
Record the aircraft you flew on, and chart your flights by aircraft family.
When you save a flight that departs within a week, FlyLog checks its status once. A manual status check now offers any schedule changes it finds.
Some badges link to a Wikipedia article about what they celebrate.
The Route tour turns the short way across the Pacific.

title: Multi-city trips and arrival times
items: Add a multi-city trip in one go, by hand or by describing it to the AI.
Record the arrival date and time of a flight.
Earn badges for the continents you have visited.
The flights table shows cities and countries instead of airport codes.
